objective: Continue investigating whether distributed gossip and independent multi-agent work can improve completed software quality and persistence, with statistical evidence for or against concrete claims and committed, pushed checkpoints between cycles.

starting_evidence.observation: Independent initial branches improved observed requirement coverage over serial revision, but only two of ten trajectories achieved full acceptance. Extra probes did not improve held-out pool selection. Some reviews exhausted without repairs; some repairs regressed earlier behavior.
starting_evidence.inference_limit: Four matched blocks from two maintained synthetic application domains do not establish general statistical superiority. Real artifact transport was simulated centrally; live autonomous gossip superiority remains untested.

questions.claim: Evidence-directed review/repair and retained source checkpoints increase whole-project acceptance while preserving inherited behavior.
questions.next_evidence: Three-arm twelve-trajectory development pilot on warehouse and job-queue applications.
questions.purpose: Debug and evaluate the controller package before freezing it for confirmation.
questions.nonclaim: Neither a routing-only causal effect nor statistical proof across software projects.

questions.claim: Independent cheap-model initial candidates improve whole-project acceptance relative to serial revision under the same frozen controller and offered call limits.
questions.next_evidence: Separate paired study across independently held-out task families, with registered practical-effect threshold, sample size, interval, and fixed stopping rule.
questions.purpose: Estimate benefit, harm, or an upper bound excluding a worthwhile benefit within the tested population.
questions.nonclaim: More repeated seeds on development fixtures are not more independent domains; favorable partial coverage alone is not completed-work superiority.

questions.claim: Peer-local gossip coordination improves accepted project completion and recovery over a fair central-orchestrator control under stated availability conditions.
questions.next_evidence: Real independently scheduled worker processes with durable local state, the same model/tool permissions, and equivalent Git, budget, and acceptance guarantees.
questions.purpose: Separate transport resilience, decision placement, and agent reasoning effects under matched fault schedules.
questions.nonclaim: A centrally stepped artifact simulation or an independent-branch coding study is not this live coordination experiment.

questions.claim: The observed effects persist when workers can use bounded coding tools rather than only return JSON proposals.
questions.next_evidence: A separately versioned tool-enabled execution contract with sandbox and budget qualification, after the core comparison is stable.
questions.purpose: Assess external validity for practical agent harnesses without silently changing the earlier experiment's interface.
questions.nonclaim: The current JSON-interface pilot cannot settle this question, and changing interface and coordination together cannot isolate either effect.

deliverables: Prospective statistical design and power calculations
cycles.gate: Focused tests, combined static gate, exact-input qualification, independent review, retained checkpoint, commit and push.

deliverables: Independent primary audit and mechanism analysis
cycles.gate: No paid dispatch until implementation, rehearsal, accounting and sufficient-funding decisions are concrete. Preserve failed, incomplete and unfavorable outcomes.

deliverables: Complete audited paired cohort with effect interval
cycles.gate: No selection of sample size or stopping after inspecting favorable effects. Report inconclusive results as inconclusive; do not keep retrying until significant.
Keep formation/controller/tool contracts matched and distinguish safety violations, infrastructure failures, incomplete work, and final acceptance.

scientific_rules: Statistical evidence concerns a named population, endpoint, effect size and execution contract; no universal proof that swarms always help or can never help is promised.
Keep development data out of confirmatory task selection and final policy tuning.
Count independent task families as the generalization unit. Repeated seeds, scenarios, milestones, and generated probes do not enlarge that count.
Specify multiplicity control before claiming either of several hypotheses wins; a claim about formation cannot be relabeled a claim about gossip.
Retain all planned runs in accounting, including bounded stops and failures; resolve infrastructure missingness under a prospectively specified rule.
Completion and inherited behavior remain primary. Speed, cost, generated-test count and source novelty are supporting measurements.
Only freeze a study after its actual execution contract passes the necessary offline and rehearsal gates. Never rewrite historical study sources or outputs.

funding.rule: No additional spending authorization is inferred from the open-ended goal. Continue useful offline work, then request any necessary cap change against a concrete reviewable execution plan.

cycle_publication.rule: Commit and push coherent verified cycles; confirm remote commit identity and retain a local receipt. Do not commit credentials, ignored raw runs, or unrelated work. A pushed development checkpoint is not evidence that the full investigation is complete.

completion_rule: The current active goal remains open while the required independent evidence and live-coordination comparison are missing. A pilot, passing harness tests, a report update, or a pushed commit is progress, not proof of the full objective.
